_circuit_breaker_check counts ALL events in db.alert_events within the window. After a breaker trip the breaker doesn't clear those events — once resumed, if old events remain inside the window the bot will be re-paused on the next tick. Consider tracking a 'last_pause_at' cursor and only counting events newer than max(window_start, last_pause_at).

_maybe_promote_winner's lead_pct uses abs(loser.pnl) as denominator; when loser.pnl == 0 the code returns spread_ok=True via the prior branch, which is correct. But for very small positive losers, lead_pct can blow up — acceptable for promote logic.

AutopilotConfigIn does not validate min_winner_lead_pct or min_lane_trades ranges — only promote_interval_hours / breaker_events / breaker_window_minutes are bounded. Add 0 ≤ min_winner_lead_pct ≤ 1000 and 1 ≤ min_lane_trades ≤ 10_000.

rca of the issue:
Minor spec gap on /api/autopilot/status:
• server.py:1426 `_autopilot_get()` returns the persisted singleton if present, else `{**DEFAULT_AUTOPILOT, '_id': 'singleton'}`.
• Once any field is persisted (e.g. via PUT /config), the doc is stored with ONLY the keys passed in payload, NOT a full schema. Subsequent GET /status returns only persisted keys — `last_promoted_at` / `last_promoted_preset` are absent until a promotion actually fires.
• Frontend handles gracefully (shows 'no promotion yet' when last_promoted_at falsy), so no visible bug, but the API contract enumerated in the iter7 spec is not strictly satisfied.
• Fix: in /api/autopilot/status, do `doc = {**DEFAULT_AUTOPILOT, **(await _autopilot_get())}` before serialization. One-line change.

Expected-failure on iter4 live-mode test:
• Bug intentionally surfaces because iteration 7 STRENGTHENED the gate from trade-key-only to full readiness (5 checks). The test currently asserts that flipping to live after providing a trade key returns 200; with iter7 it now returns 409 listing Telegram + Worker as remaining blockers. This is the desired security posture — the test is outdated.
